title: Dependency heatmap + priority-bucketing to auto-allocate launch runway and capacity credits
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Problem: As we scale cross-surface launches (runtime, console, API), manually assigning launch windows and capacity credits has created uneven load, blocked dependent teams, and increased rollback incidents. We lack a single, observable view that combines interservice dependencies, team-level readiness signals, and capacity runway to automatically suggest launch priority buckets and a recommended allocation of capacity credits and guardrails.

Goal: Deliver an actionable "Launch Allocation Engine" prototype that produces a dependency heatmap and recommended priority buckets for a slate of features. The output should be consumable by PMs and Release Leads (CSV / UI) and should integrate with the Console launch calendar and Runtime capacity forecast dashboards. This work will reduce manual alignment time pre-launch, lower contention between Runtime and Dedicated capacity reservations, and reduce last-minute rollbacks due to under-provisioning.

Scope: Phase 1 (this ticket) will: 1) define the scoring model and signals for interservice dependency impact and runway fragility; 2) build a dependency heatmap export (CSV + queryable Confluence link) and a UI prototype wireframe for Console; 3) produce recommended priority buckets (High/Medium/Low) and suggested capacity-credit allocations for release-train owners; 4) document rollout playbook and acceptance criteria. Not in scope: full autoscheduler enforcement or automatic ticket gating (Phase 2).

Signals considered: dependency graph from GitHub PRs and owned services, readiness flags (tests passing, infra e2e status), capacity forecasts from Runtime telemetry (per-model QPS and token forecasts), Dedicated reservations, SLO risk score, and external sales/regulatory deadlines.
acceptance_criteria: Scoring model doc published with inputs, weighting, and example outputs (Confluence link) and reviewed by Runtime/Console/Platform.
Dependency heatmap export available for a sample slate (CSV) with at least 30 features from three teams and annotated risk bands.
Priority bucket recommendations (High/Medium/Low) generated for the sample slate with suggested capacity-credit allocations and rationale.
Prototype wireframe added to Console mockups with a readout panel and CSV import option.
Playbook describing human-in-the-loop review steps, escalation paths, and rollback triggers published and validated in a dry-run rehearsal.
risks: Signal gaps: incomplete dependency graph (missing 3rd-party integrations) could skew recommendations.
Model bias: weighting choices may favor throughput-heavy services and under-prioritize customer-impacting UI fixes.
Operational churn: teams may treat recommendations as prescriptive rather than advisory, increasing tension during cutover.
Data freshness: capacity forecasts older than 24h reduce accuracy; requires telemetry SLA from Runtime team.
decision_log: 2025-01-12: Chosen scoring baseline that combines SLO-risk(40%), capacity-runway-fragility(30%), dependency-degree(20%), and external-deadline(10%) — approved by PM leads.
2025-01-20: Agreed to surface recommendations as advisory buckets (not automated gating) for Phase 1 — reduces risk of accidental enforcement.
2025-01-28: Decided to export CSV + Confluence readout rather than building full Console backend integration in Phase 1 to accelerate iteration.
